import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

def solve(prices, split_factors):
    # Ensure prices and split_factors have the same shape and index
    if prices.shape != split_factors.shape:
        raise ValueError("prices and split_factors must have the same shape")
    
    # Calculate the forward-adjusted close prices
    adjusted_prices = prices * split_factors
    
    # Initialize the weights DataFrame with zeros
    weights = pd.DataFrame(np.zeros_like(prices), index=prices.index, columns=prices.columns)
    
    # Iterate over each column (asset) and calculate the weights
    for col in prices.columns:
        # Get the price series for the current asset
        price_series = adjusted_prices[col]
        
        # Calculate the returns for the last 21 days
        returns = price_series.pct_change().dropna()
        
        # Calculate the sample standard deviation of the returns
        std_dev = returns.std(ddof=1)
        
        # Calculate the momentum signal
        momentum_signal = np.sign(price_series / price_series.shift(21) - 1)
        
        # Calculate the scaling factor
        scaling_factor = np.minimum(1, 0.10 / (std_dev * np.sqrt(252)))
        
        # Calculate the raw weights
        raw_weights = momentum_signal * scaling_factor
        
        # Normalize the weights to sum to 1/4
        normalized_weights = raw_weights / raw_weights.sum() * 0.25
        
        # Assign the normalized weights to the corresponding positions in the weights DataFrame
        weights.loc[returns.index, col] = normalized_weights
    
    # Set the weights for the first 20 rows to zero
    weights.iloc[:20] = 0
    
    # Replace any non-finite values with zero
    weights = weights.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], 0)
    
    # Ensure all weights are within the range [0, 1]
    weights = weights.clip(lower=0, upper=1)
    
    return weights
